source_scope.use: WEB wording and local canonical coordinates decide the coverage surface. OSHB and UXLC verse, clause, morphology, accent, and word markers corroborate literary observations only and do not select a reading, translation, speaker identity, theology, or boundary.

read: local OSHB Hosea XML as marker evidence
local UXLC Hosea XML as marker evidence
Daniel completed literary artifact property names for schema shape only

summary.principle: Prefer the complete enacted sign, accusation-to-consequence movement, recollection-to-appeal sequence, question/image chain, or judgment-restoration diptych. Treat chapter numbers, famous verses, individual metaphors, and source-language metadata as insufficient by themselves to force a seam.

global_guards: Every proposed unit is a retrieval candidate, not reviewed gold or canonical text.
No title or speaker description decides theology, identity, authorship, date, historicity, ethics, fulfillment, covenant system, monarchy chronology, or divine psychology.

The WEB-to-MT offset is explicit: WEB Hos.1.10-1.11 corresponds to MT Hos.2.1-2.2; WEB Hos.2.1-2.23 corresponds to MT Hos.2.3-2.25; WEB Hos.13.16 corresponds to MT Hos.14.1; WEB Hos.14.1-14.9 corresponds to MT Hos.14.2-14.10.
Original-language markers corroborate form and discourse observations only. Roots, lemma numbers, morphology, accents, and source labels are not meanings or boundary authority.
Single-verse units occur only for the superscription and the demonstrably wisdom-like closing colophon, not because a verse is famous.
Holds concern presentation and retrieval integrity only; no hold asks a reviewer to settle theology or an actor's identity.

proposed_units.title: The Word to Hosea in the Days of the Kings
proposed_units.literary_form: prophetic superscription
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Collection-heading voice identifies the word, prophetic recipient, and royal-era frame; no narrative scene has begun.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: One-line superscription; no refrain.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.1.2 resets from heading to narrated commission with 'When Yahweh spoke at first by Hosea'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The complete heading formula 'Yahweh's word that came to Hosea' plus the paired Judah and Israel regnal notices closes before the first narrated command.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.1.1 begins with the construct heading dbr-YHWH and preserves the full regnal chain; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: That span would merge the paratext-like prophetic heading with the first enacted-sign command even though Hos.1.2 supplies a new temporal formula, reported speech, and imperative scene.

proposed_units.title: The First Sign and the Bow Broken at Jezreel
proposed_units.literary_form: enacted sign narrative with naming oracle
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Third-person prophetic narration frames a command to Hosea, its enactment, and a divine naming speech concerning Jezreel and Israel.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Commission and enactment in Hos.1.2-1.3; naming-and-consequence oracle in Hos.1.4-1.5.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.1.6 starts a new conception/birth cycle with 'She conceived again, and bore a daughter'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The command 'Go, take', the fulfillment 'So he went and took', and 'Call his name Jezreel' form a complete sign-to-interpretation chain ending with the bow broken in the valley.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.1.2-1.5 preserves the commission, wayyiqtol enactment chain, naming imperative, and concluding day formula; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Splitting before Hos.1.4 would detach the child's birth from the naming oracle that gives the enacted sign its literary function.

proposed_units.title: Lo-Ruhamah and the Judah Counterpoint
proposed_units.literary_form: naming oracle with contrastive counter-oracle
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Narrated birth moves directly into divine naming speech; the speech contrasts the house of Israel with the house of Judah without requiring a historical or theological ruling.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Name-and-consequence stanza followed by a tightly attached 'But I will have mercy' counterpoint.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.1.8 begins the next child's conception only after Lo-Ruhamah is weaned.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The new birth formula and 'Call her name Lo-Ruhamah' govern both the no-mercy sentence and the immediately contrastive 'But I will have mercy on the house of Judah'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.1.6-1.7 preserves the naming imperative and adversative Judah clause inside one reported speech; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Making Hos.1.7 an orphan counter-oracle would sever the explicit adversative contrast from the Lo-Ruhamah naming speech it qualifies.

proposed_units.title: Lo-Ammi Reversed into One People
proposed_units.literary_form: enacted naming sign with reversal oracle and responsive summons
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Narrated third birth leads into divine naming speech, then a future reversal concerning Israel and Judah, capped by commands to address brothers and sisters.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Birth/name stanza in Hos.1.8-1.9; reversal in Hos.1.10-1.11; name-reversal summons in Hos.2.1.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.2.2 changes to the forensic imperative 'Contend with your mother', opening the marital lawsuit.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The negated name 'not my people' is answered by 'sons of the living God', one gathered people, the renewed Jezreel name, and the paired imperatives 'Say ... My people ... My loved one'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.1.8-1.9 plus Hos.2.1-2.3 exposes the English/MT offset while preserving the name-reversal chain; locators are evidence only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: That split would isolate judgment from the deliberate reversal of the same child's name; the larger sign movement is the safer retrieval object.

proposed_units.title: Contend with the Mother Who Forgot
proposed_units.literary_form: marital lawsuit accusation-to-consequence movement
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A forensic command addresses children concerning their mother; first-person divine speech accumulates accusation, threatened exposure, deprivation, and remembered neglect.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Contention and warning Hos.2.2-2.5; blocked pursuit Hos.2.6-2.7; gift-misrecognition and deprivation Hos.2.8-2.13.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.2.14 repeats 'Therefore behold' but reverses its force from obstruction and stripping to alluring and tender speech.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The opening double 'Contend' controls the causal chain of 'lest', 'for', and repeated 'therefore/I will' clauses through the closure 'went after her lovers and forgot me, says Yahweh'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.2.4-2.15 preserves the vocative/legal imperatives, causal particles, pursuit-return speech, and closing messenger formula; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The second half supplies the reason and enacted consequences of the first; splitting would weaken the complete accusation-to-consequence lawsuit movement.

proposed_units.title: Allure, Betroth, Answer, and Sow
proposed_units.literary_form: restoration promise with betrothal and response chain
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: First-person divine promise addresses the estranged woman/people in the discourse's surface imagery; identity and doctrine remain outside this boundary decision.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Wilderness courtship Hos.2.14-2.15; 'in that day' renaming and peace Hos.2.16-2.18; triple betrothal Hos.2.19-2.20; cascading response and name reversal Hos.2.21-2.23.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.3.1 opens a new narrated command, 'Yahweh said to me, Go again'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The pivot 'Therefore behold, I will allure her' initiates repeated promises, 'in that day' stanzas, 'I will betroth' anaphora, the heaven-earth-produce response chain, and exact reversal of Lo-Ruhamah/Lo-Ammi.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.2.16-2.25 preserves the discourse pivot, day formulae, repeated betrothal verbs, response chain, and name reversals; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The cosmic response and sowing/name reversal are the harvest of the preceding restored relationship and should hydrate as the same promise movement.

proposed_units.title: Go Again: Bought Love and the Many Days
proposed_units.literary_form: enacted restoration sign with interpretive oracle
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: First-person prophet reports a divine command, purchase, address to the woman, and an explanatory future concerning Israel.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Command and analogy Hos.3.1; enactment and direct address Hos.3.2-3.3; interpretive 'many days/afterward' oracle Hos.3.4-3.5.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.4.1 abandons sign narrative for a public lawsuit summons, 'Hear Yahweh's word, you children of Israel'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The command 'Go again, love', its first-person fulfillment 'I bought', the probationary address, and the paired 'many days/Afterward' explanation form one sign-act sequence.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.3.1-3.5 preserves command, first-person enactment, direct speech, causal interpretation, and final afterward clause; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The latter verses explicitly interpret the duration and direction of the enacted sign; detaching them would reduce both narrative and oracle coherence.

proposed_units.title: Hear the Charge and the Mourning Land
proposed_units.literary_form: lawsuit summons, accusation list, and cosmic consequence
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Prophetic summons addresses the children of Israel and announces Yahweh's charge against inhabitants of the land.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Charge and missing virtues Hos.4.1; transgression catalogue Hos.4.2; land-and-creature consequence Hos.4.3.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.4.4 turns from inhabitants generally to a difficult second-person dispute involving priestly accusation.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The forensic formula 'Hear ... for Yahweh has a charge' is answered by 'Therefore the land will mourn', completing summons, evidence, and consequence.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.4.1-4.3 preserves the opening plural imperative, controversy term, negated virtue triad, transgression chain, and therefore consequence; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.4.3 is the expressly signaled consequence of the charges and would become an orphan ecological image if separated.

proposed_units.title: Like People, Like Priest
proposed_units.literary_form: priestly accusation and reciprocal consequence oracle
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Difficult direct address moves through priest/people language, rejection of knowledge, and mirrored punishment; exact addressee identity is not decided.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Disputed accusation Hos.4.4-4.5; rejected knowledge and law Hos.4.6; priestly appetite and reciprocal judgment Hos.4.7-4.10.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.4.11 starts a compact vice maxim, 'Prostitution, wine, and new wine take away understanding', then broadens to divination and sexual-cult accusation.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The reciprocal formulas 'Because you have rejected ... I will reject', 'Because you have forgotten ... I will forget', and 'like people, like priest' bind the difficult opening to the eat-but-not-enough consequence.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.4.4-4.10 preserves second/third-person shifts and repeated knowledge/reject/forget/punish correspondences; difficult syntax lowers confidence but does not authorize emendation.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.4.7-4.10 develops the same priestly rejection into shame, appetite, and reciprocal punishment; the internal stanza is better retained under one parent unit.

proposed_units.title: Understanding Taken and the People Brought to Ruin
proposed_units.literary_form: vice maxim expanded into cultic accusation and consequence
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Prophetic accusation describes impaired understanding, divination, hilltop sacrifice, and reciprocal sexual misconduct; the final consequence addresses the people as a whole.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Maxim Hos.4.11; idolatrous inquiry Hos.4.12; hilltop practice and family consequence Hos.4.13-4.14.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.4.15 turns to direct warning: 'Though you, Israel ... don't let Judah offend'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The opening triad 'Prostitution, wine, and new wine' is resumed by 'spirit of prostitution' and closes with the people-without-understanding ruin, forming an inclusio.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.4.11-4.14 preserves the heart/understanding loss, recurring prostitution root, consultation language, and therefore consequence; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The mountain practices are the concrete expansion of the preceding divination/infidelity charge, and the final lack-of-understanding verdict closes the opening maxim.

proposed_units.title: Do Not Come to Beth Aven
proposed_units.literary_form: warning oracle with stubborn-animal and wind verdicts
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Direct warning distinguishes Israel and Judah at the surface, then describes Israel/Ephraim with heifer, idol, drink, and wind images.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Prohibitive warning Hos.4.15; stubborn-heifer question Hos.4.16; Ephraim/idol abandonment and wind consequence Hos.4.17-4.19.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.5.1 introduces a fresh triple hearing summons to priests, Israel, and the royal house.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The prohibitions 'don't let ... don't come ... neither go ... nor swear' initiate a compact warning that terminates in the wind-wrapped disappointment of the sacrifices.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.4.15-4.19 preserves the negative imperatives, Judah/Israel contrast, Ephraim naming, and closing wind image; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The drink and wind couplet concludes the same Ephraim-idol warning; a two-verse image split would over-weight metaphor changes over the continuing verdict.

proposed_units.title: Priests, Israel, and the House of the King
proposed_units.literary_form: leadership summons and failed-seeking judgment
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A threefold public summons addresses priests, Israel, and the royal house; divine first-person knowledge and judgment lead to futile cultic seeking.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Leadership indictment Hos.5.1-5.3; deeds prevent return Hos.5.4-5.5; failed seeking and new-moon consequence Hos.5.6-5.7.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.5.8 starts a geographic battle-alarm with horn, trumpet, and battle cry imperatives.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The repeated 'Listen ... listen ... give ear' and 'judgment is against you' govern the snare imagery, pride/stumbling, and climactic failure to find the withdrawn deity.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.5.1-5.7 preserves the three imperatival addressees, judgment formula, repeated knowledge language, stumble chain, and failed seeking; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The deeds, pride, stumbling, and failed seeking are the consequence movement of the leadership summons rather than a new oracle.

proposed_units.title: Sound the Alarm: Moth, Rot, and Lion
proposed_units.literary_form: battle-alarm oracle escalating from decay to predation and withdrawal
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A warning cry moves across named locations and both Ephraim and Judah; first-person divine judgment uses moth, rot, sickness, wound, and lion images.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Alarm and desolation Hos.5.8-5.10; oppression and slow decay Hos.5.11-5.12; failed foreign healing and lion attack Hos.5.13-5.15.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.6.1 changes voice and mood to first-person plural exhortation, 'Come! Let's return to Yahweh'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: Horn/trumpet imperatives open the oracle; the imagery intensifies from moth/rottenness to incurable wound and lion, ending with deliberate withdrawal 'until they acknowledge ... and seek'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.5.8-5.15 preserves the alarm imperatives, Judah/Ephraim parallelism, disease lexicon, lion repetition, and final until-clause; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The foreign-healing episode and lion judgment complete the sickness/decay trajectory introduced in Hos.5.11-5.12; splitting would obscure the escalation.

proposed_units.title: Come, Let Us Return and Press On to Know
proposed_units.literary_form: communal return summons and healing confession
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: An embedded first-person plural voice summons a community to return; the unit's sincerity, identity, and theological adequacy are not boundary questions.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Return/heal couplet Hos.6.1; revival hope Hos.6.2; acknowledge/know and rain similes Hos.6.3.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.6.4 answers with direct divine vocatives and rhetorical questions to Ephraim and Judah.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The paired cohortative-style appeals 'Come! Let's return' and 'Let's acknowledge ... Let's press on' create a self-contained communal speech framed by healing and rain images.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.6.1-6.3 preserves the opening plural imperatives/cohortatives, return root, paired tear/heal verbs, and knowledge/rain closure; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.5.15 is divine first-person withdrawal, while Hos.6.1 begins an overt first-person plural quoted response; preserving adjacent units retains the call-and-response seam without conflating voices.

proposed_units.title: Morning-Cloud Love and the Blood-Stained Road
proposed_units.literary_form: divine lament-question followed by prophetic indictment
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Direct divine questions address Ephraim and Judah, then first-person judgment recalls prophetic words and surveys covenant breach, Gilead, priests, and defiled Israel.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Vanishing-love questions Hos.6.4; word-judgment and mercy/knowledge criterion Hos.6.5-6.6; breach and violent-place catalogue Hos.6.7-6.10.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.6.11 turns again to Judah and opens the harvest/restoration/healing hinge that crosses into Hos.7.1.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The doubled 'What shall I do to you?' and morning-cloud/dew similes govern the explanation 'Therefore I have cut them ... with the words of my mouth' through the concluding 'Israel is defiled'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.6.4-6.10 preserves the double vocative question, fleeting-mist comparison, therefore relation, mercy/knowledge parallel, and place/violence catalogue; difficult Hos.6.5 and Hos.6.7 remain evidence-sensitive.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The place and priest accusations substantiate the divine lament's charge of transient loyalty; a child split may be useful, but the complete lament-to-indictment unit should remain primary.

proposed_units.title: Harvest, Restoration, and the Healing That Uncovers
proposed_units.literary_form: cross-chapter judgment-healing hinge
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person speech addresses Judah, then turns to healing Israel while exposing Ephraim/Samaria; speaker continuity is surface-level and no identity theory is imposed.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Judah harvest line Hos.6.11; temporal restoration/healing linkage Hos.6.11b-7.1; remembered deeds and engulfment Hos.7.2.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.7.3 begins a court scene: wickedness and lies make king and princes glad.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The temporal clauses 'when I restore the fortunes of my people' and 'When I would heal Israel' bridge the chapter boundary, while Hos.7.2 closes with deeds engulfing them 'before my face'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.6.11-7.2 preserves the Judah harvest clause followed by two first-person temporal/remembering clauses; syntax supports a hinge but does not settle every punctuation option.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: That chapter-shaped split would detach 'when I restore' from 'when I would heal' and suppress the cross-chapter rhetorical hinge; the exact attachment remains presentation-contested, so the larger hinge is held.

proposed_units.title: The King's Day and the Oven of Conspiracy
proposed_units.literary_form: court accusation built as an oven-image stanza
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A royal-court scene describes king, princes, mockers, judges, and fallen kings; the actors' historical identities are not required for the unit.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Court corruption Hos.7.3; oven comparison Hos.7.4; king's-day intoxication Hos.7.5; oven ambush and devoured judges Hos.7.6-7.7.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.7.8 shifts from the court to Ephraim among the nations and begins the unturned-pancake image.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The repeated oven/fire language at Hos.7.4, Hos.7.6, and Hos.7.7 encloses the king's-day scene and terminates in fallen kings and the refrain-like failure to call.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.7.3-7.7 preserves king/prince/judge terms and the repeated oven, heat, smolder, morning, and devour lexicon; difficult syntax remains corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Both spans are one sustained oven simile surrounding the royal festival and conspiracy; division at night/morning would atomize the image's temporal development.

proposed_units.title: An Unturned Cake That Does Not Realize
proposed_units.literary_form: nation-image accusation with repeated unawareness refrain
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Ephraim is described among the nations through food, aging, and pride images.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Mixed/unturned image Hos.7.8; devoured strength and gray hairs Hos.7.9; pride testimony and non-return Hos.7.10.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.7.11 opens a new explicit simile, 'Ephraim is like an easily deceived dove'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The twice-repeated 'he doesn't realize it' binds swallowed strength and gray hairs to the pride/non-return verdict.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.7.8-7.10 preserves the Ephraim anaphora, mixed/food image, repeated non-knowledge clause, pride-testimony refrain, and no-return close; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.7.10 is the evaluative close to the repeated unawareness, not a standalone pride proof-text.

proposed_units.title: The Deceived Dove and the Faulty Bow
proposed_units.literary_form: political-religious lament framed by animal and weapon similes
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person speech laments Ephraim's calls to Egypt and Assyria, false cries, defection, and plots.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Dove/net movement Hos.7.11-7.12; woe and false speech Hos.7.13-7.15; faulty-bow and Egypt derision Hos.7.16.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.8.1 commands a fresh trumpet blast and announces an eagle over Yahweh's house.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The dove simile and divine net open the stanza; repeated 'from/against me' accusations lead to the faulty-bow comparison and final Egypt derision.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.7.11-7.16 preserves the dove/bird/net field, woe exclamation, repeated first-person object/suffixes, return language, and bow comparison; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The bed-howling, grain assembly, plotting, and faulty bow are the evidence for the dove stanza's woe, so the accusation-consequence movement should remain intact.

proposed_units.title: Trumpet, Covenant Cry, and the Calf of Samaria
proposed_units.literary_form: alarm oracle with covenant charge and idol indictment
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A trumpet-bearing addressee is commanded; divine first-person speech answers Israel's acknowledgment claim with accusations concerning good, kings, princes, and the calf.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Alarm and covenant charge Hos.8.1; protested acknowledgment and pursuit Hos.8.2-8.3; rulers/idols and calf taunt Hos.8.4-8.6.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.8.7 begins the proverb-like sowing/reaping consequence chain.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The trumpet command and eagle threat frame the charge; Israel's 'My God ... acknowledge you' is rebutted through kings and calf until 'the calf of Samaria shall be broken'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.8.1-8.6 preserves trumpet imperative, covenant/law pairing, cry formula, first-person denials, calf repetition, and no-god verdict; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The unauthorized kings and made calf specify how the covenant/law rebellion contradicts the acknowledgment cry; keeping the rebuttal together is more coherent.

proposed_units.title: Sowing Wind and Being Swallowed among Nations
proposed_units.literary_form: sowing-reaping proverb expanded into national consequence
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Third-person prophetic indictment moves from failed agriculture to Israel among nations, Assyrian pursuit, and costly alliances.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Wind/whirlwind and crop failure Hos.8.7; swallowed/worthless nation Hos.8.8; wild donkey and hired lovers Hos.8.9-8.10.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.8.11 returns to cultic accusation with the repeated noun 'altars'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The causal 'For they sow the wind' governs the escalating swallowing field: no grain, strangers swallow yield, Israel swallowed, and political self-sale among nations.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.8.7-8.10 preserves sow/reap parallelism, swallow repetition, nation/Assyria terms, and gather/oppression close; the difficult Hos.8.10 wording lowers no boundary by itself.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The famous sow/reap line introduces the entire swallowing consequence chain and should not be isolated as a proverb-sized proof-text.

proposed_units.title: Altars, Written Instruction, and Devouring Fire
proposed_units.literary_form: cultic accusation-consequence oracle
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Ephraim, Israel, and Judah are addressed/described through altars, written instruction, sacrifice, palaces, fortified cities, and fire.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Multiplied altars Hos.8.11; rejected written instruction Hos.8.12; unacceptable sacrifice and remembered guilt Hos.8.13; forgotten Maker and fire Hos.8.14.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.9.1 begins a direct festival warning, 'Don't rejoice, Israel'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: Altars 'for sinning' and instruction regarded as strange generate the sacrifice-not-accepted verdict, remembered iniquity, and closing fire on cities and fortresses.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.8.11-8.14 preserves altar/sin repetition, writing/law terms, sacrifice/eat language, remember/forget contrast, and fire consequence; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.8.14's 'For Israel has forgotten' supplies the concluding reason and broadens the same cultic-memory indictment to building and fire; it is not a detached Judah oracle.

proposed_units.title: No Festival Joy in the Land of Exile
proposed_units.literary_form: festival warning and exile consequence
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Direct warning addresses Israel, then describes failed threshing, lost land, polluted food, impossible feast observance, flight, burial, and desolated tents.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Prohibition and threshing-floor accusation Hos.9.1-9.2; land/exile and impure offerings Hos.9.3-9.4; feast-day question and Egypt/Memphis consequence Hos.9.5-9.6.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.9.7 announces 'The days of visitation ... reckoning have come' and turns to prophet/watchman hostility.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The opening 'Don't rejoice' and harvest/festival lexicon are inverted through failed produce, no acceptable offerings, the rhetorical feast-day question, and burial away from home.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.9.1-9.6 preserves negative joy imperative, threshing/wine terms, land/return, offering/feast vocabulary, rhetorical question, and Egypt/Memphis burial; difficult Hos.9.6 does not force a smaller unit.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The feast-day question and burial answer complete the festival warning; separation would leave the question without the preceding loss of acceptable worship.

proposed_units.title: Days of Reckoning and the Snared Watchman
proposed_units.literary_form: visitation announcement with contested prophet-watchman stanza
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A prophetic voice announces reckoning and reports hostility around prophet/watchman language; exact voice alignment in Hos.9.7-9.8 is not decided.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Doubled day announcement Hos.9.7; prophet/watchman and snare Hos.9.7-9.8; Gibeah comparison and remembered punishment Hos.9.9.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.9.10 starts divine first-person recollection, 'I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The repeated 'days ... have come' opens a compact reckoning stanza; hostility/snare language culminates in the Gibeah analogy and repeated 'remember/punish' sentence.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.9.7-9.9 preserves day/visitation repetition, prophet/watchman terms, hostility/snare field, Gibeah comparison, and remember/punish close; syntax supports a stanza but not one uncontested speaker layout.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.9.9 provides the historical-comparative verdict and punishment closure for the hostility/snare stanza; the unit is held because presentation inside Hos.9.7-9.8 remains contestable, not because Gibeah's identity must be settled.

proposed_units.title: Wilderness Grapes and the Withered Future
proposed_units.literary_form: recollection-to-barrenness lament
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person recollection of finding Israel/fathers moves into Ephraim's loss of children and a brief petition addressed to Yahweh.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Grapes/first fig and Baal Peor recollection Hos.9.10; flying glory and no-birth chain Hos.9.11-9.13; anguished 'what will you give?' petition Hos.9.14.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.9.15 relocates the accusation to Gilgal and resumes first-person judgment with 'there I hated them'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The found-fruit images reverse into no birth, pregnancy, or conception; the prophet-like petition 'Yahweh, what will you give?' is the lament's climax rather than a separate oracle.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.9.10-9.14 preserves first-person find/see verbs, first-fruit imagery, birth/conception/womb/breast field, and the interrupted petition; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The one-verse petition voices the preceding bereavement crisis and should not be atomized; its interruption is a climactic lament turn inside the same movement.

proposed_units.title: Gilgal's Rebellion and the Wandering Coda
proposed_units.literary_form: place-centered judgment oracle with prophetic coda
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person judgment at Gilgal and Ephraim's dried root is followed by a surface speaker shift, 'My God will cast them away'.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Gilgal/house expulsion Hos.9.15; root-fruit-child reversal Hos.9.16; prophetic non-listening/wandering coda Hos.9.17.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.10.1 begins a new vine-and-fruit saying about Israel.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The wickedness/rebellion at Gilgal yields root, fruit, and offspring destruction; Hos.9.17 restates the verdict because 'they didn't listen', closing rather than reopening the movement.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.9.15-9.17 preserves Gilgal/house language, rebel rulers, struck root/no fruit, speaker-surface shift to 'my God', and wandering-among-nations close; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Although Hos.9.17 changes the surface speaker, it is a short summarizing coda that repeats rejection and gives the oracle its final wandering consequence.

proposed_units.title: Luxuriant Vine, Empty King, and the Calf Carried Away
proposed_units.literary_form: cult-monarchy judgment sequence
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Israel/Samaria are described through vine, divided heart, empty royal speech, poisonous judgment, calf panic, deportation, floating king, and ruined high places.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Vine/altars and divided heart Hos.10.1-10.2; no-king speech and false covenant Hos.10.3-10.4; calf procession and royal shame Hos.10.5-10.7; altar destruction and mountain cry Hos.10.8.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.10.9 shifts to direct second-person historical address, 'Israel, you have sinned from the days of Gibeah'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: Fruit multiplied altars; divided heart yields demolished altars; no-king speech yields false covenant; calf and king are then carried/floated away before the mountain cry closes the sequence.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.10.1-10.8 preserves vine/fruit/altar repetitions, divided-heart guilt, quoted king speech, calf/king deportation field, and high-place destruction; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The calf and high-place collapse are the concrete cultic consequence of the vine/altar and false-covenant diagnosis; the macro sequence should remain retrievable as one.

proposed_units.title: From Gibeah to Fallow Ground to Daybreak
proposed_units.literary_form: recollection-appeal-judgment triptych
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Direct address to Israel/Ephraim/Judah moves from Gibeah recollection to agricultural summons and then battle consequence.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Gibeah recollection and chastisement Hos.10.9-10.10; heifer/plowing scene and positive sow-seek appeal Hos.10.11-10.12; wicked sowing and battle harvest Hos.10.13-10.15.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.11.1 begins a parental first-person recollection, 'When Israel was a child, then I loved him'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The field vocabulary binds the middle: thresh, plow, break clods, sow, reap, fallow ground; it is deliberately answered by 'You have plowed wickedness ... reaped iniquity' and a war harvest.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.10.9-10.15 preserves Gibeah recurrence, discipline/binding, heifer/plow/sow/reap field, imperative appeal, and therefore battle consequence; difficult Hos.10.10 does not force atomization.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Isolating the famous sow-in-righteousness verse would destroy the designed contrast between the appeal and the immediately reversed plowing/reaping judgment.

proposed_units.title: The Child Taught to Walk Yet Bent Away
proposed_units.literary_form: parental recollection turning to refusal and consequence
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person recollection describes child, teaching, healing, cords, feeding, refusal to return, Assyrian rule, sword, and settled turning-away.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Loved/called child Hos.11.1-11.2; taught/healed/drew/fed Hos.11.3-11.4; refused return and sword Hos.11.5-11.7.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.11.8 interrupts consequence with a fourfold compassion question, 'How can I give you up?'
proposed_units.deciding_marker: Repeated first-person caregiving verbs in Hos.11.1-11.4 are answered by the refusal-to-return and sword sequence in Hos.11.5-11.7, completing recollection-to-consequence.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.11.1-11.7 preserves child/call, teach/heal, cords/love, feed, return/refuse, sword, and bent-turning language; difficult Hos.11.3-11.4 remains corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The consequence stanza is the direct reversal of the parental care recollection; retaining the full movement avoids sentimental proof-texting of either half.

proposed_units.title: How Can I Give You Up?
proposed_units.literary_form: compassion question chain and restoration promise
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person speech directly addresses Ephraim/Israel, moves through internal reversal language, then promises a lion-like call and trembling return.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Fourfold question and compassion turn Hos.11.8; restraint declaration Hos.11.9; lion roar and return from west/Egypt/Assyria Hos.11.10-11.11.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.11.12 abruptly resumes accusation: 'Ephraim surrounds me with falsehood'.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The repeated 'How can I' questions turn the preceding threat, and repeated 'I will not' declarations lead to the lion roar, trembling children, settled houses, and closing messenger formula.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.11.8-11.11 preserves the four interrogatives, inward-turn/compassion terms, negative first-person declarations, lion roar, trembling motion, and messenger close; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The returning children are the narrative consequence of the compassion/restraint question chain, so the judgment-restoration turn should stay whole.

proposed_units.title: Falsehood Around Me and Wind Pursued
proposed_units.literary_form: cross-chapter accusation couplet
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person accusation names Ephraim/Israel/Judah, followed by third-person Ephraim indictment concerning wind, lies, Assyria, and Egypt.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Falsehood/deceit Hos.11.12; wind/lies/desolation and foreign covenant Hos.12.1.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.12.2 explicitly opens a controversy with Judah and moves into Jacob recollection.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: Falsehood and deceit in Hos.11.12 continue as multiplied lies in Hos.12.1; the Assyria/Egypt pair closes the accusation before the new controversy formula.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.11.12-12.1 preserves Ephraim anaphora, falsehood/deceit/lies field, and the paired Assyria/Egypt actions across the chapter seam; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Chapter division would sever the lexical falsehood/lie continuation, while Hos.12.2's explicit controversy formula is the stronger new-unit marker.

proposed_units.title: The Controversy with Jacob and the Call to Return
proposed_units.literary_form: lawsuit recollection culminating in appeal
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A controversy with Judah/Jacob recalls womb, struggle, weeping, Bethel, and the divine name, then directly summons return, kindness, justice, and waiting.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Controversy/verdict Hos.12.2; Jacob recollection Hos.12.3-12.5; therefore appeal Hos.12.6.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.12.7 shifts to a merchant with dishonest scales and an Ephraim wealth boast.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The explicit controversy formula leads through ancestor recollection to the inferential imperative 'Therefore turn to your God', making recollection and appeal inseparable.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.12.2-12.6 preserves controversy/repay, Jacob name and heel/struggle field, Bethel, divine-name formula, and therefore-return imperative; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.12.6 is the explicit rhetorical conclusion of the Jacob recollection and should not become an isolated moral maxim.

proposed_units.title: Dishonest Scales and the Tent-Making Rebuttal
proposed_units.literary_form: merchant accusation and boast answered by exodus-prophet oracle
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A merchant figure and Ephraim's wealth boast are answered by divine first-person self-identification, tent promise, prophets/visions, and altar judgment.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Dishonest scales and boast Hos.12.7-12.8; divine Egypt/tent rebuttal Hos.12.9; prophet/vision mediation Hos.12.10; Gilead/Gilgal altar verdict Hos.12.11.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.12.12 begins a fresh Jacob-in-Aram recollection paired with prophetic exodus preservation.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The boast 'I have become rich' is directly countered by 'But I am Yahweh your God from the land of Egypt'; tents, prophets, and worthless altars extend that rebuttal.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.12.7-12.11 preserves the difficult merchant/Canaan term, scale/deceit field, wealth boast, adversative divine self-identification, tents, prophets/visions, and altar heaps; no lexical choice is authorized.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The divine self-identification and tent/prophet/altar sequence is the direct rebuttal to the wealth-and-innocence boast; separating accusation from answer weakens the dialogue.

proposed_units.title: A Wife Tended, a People Preserved, Anger Repaid
proposed_units.literary_form: ancestor-prophet recollection with judgment conclusion
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Third-person recollection juxtaposes Jacob's service for a wife with Israel's exodus preservation by a prophet, then names Ephraim's provocation and repayment.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Jacob service Hos.12.12; prophet-led deliverance/preservation Hos.12.13; Ephraim blood/contempt consequence Hos.12.14.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.13.1 opens a new Ephraim rise-and-death retrospect.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The repeated 'for a wife/by a prophet' service-preservation parallel is capped by 'Therefore' repayment in the WEB logic, producing a compact recollection-verdict unit.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.12.12-12.14 preserves Jacob/Israel naming, wife/tend repetition, prophet anaphora, preserve verb, and bitter-provocation repayment; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.12.14 supplies the verdict against which the paired recollections function; detaching it would leave the comparison rhetorically unresolved.

proposed_units.title: Ephraim Exalted, Guilty, and Gone Like Mist
proposed_units.literary_form: rise-death retrospect with vanishing-image chain
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Prophetic retrospect describes Ephraim's former elevation, guilt through Baal, increasing idol-making, and four images of disappearance.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Rise/guilt/death Hos.13.1; intensified idol accusation Hos.13.2; mist/dew/chaff/smoke consequence Hos.13.3.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.13.4 changes to direct divine first-person self-identification from Egypt.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The compressed 'exalted ... guilty ... died' sequence expands into 'sin more and more' and culminates in the fourfold 'Therefore they will be like' disappearance chain.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.13.1-13.3 preserves Ephraim speech/exaltation/guilt/death sequence, increasing-sin wording, crafted idols, and mist/dew/chaff/smoke comparison chain; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.13.3 is the expressly marked consequence of the rise-to-idolatry accusation and should not be isolated as an image anthology.

proposed_units.title: Known in the Wilderness, Met by the Wild Beasts
proposed_units.literary_form: provider recollection reversed into predator judgment
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person address recalls Egypt, wilderness knowledge, pasture and satisfaction, then turns to lion, leopard, bear, and wild-animal attack.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Divine self-identification Hos.13.4; wilderness/pasture care and forgetting Hos.13.5-13.6; predator chain Hos.13.7-13.8.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.13.9 turns to a direct ruin/helper verdict and then a king-question sequence.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The remembered provider 'I knew you ... they were filled' is reversed by 'Therefore I am like a lion', launching a sustained predator chain rather than independent animal metaphors.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.13.4-13.8 preserves Egypt self-identification, know/savior, wilderness/pasture/fill/forget, therefore, and lion/leopard/bear/wild-animal chain; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The predator judgment is the explicit 'Therefore' reversal of provision and forgetting; keeping provider-to-predator movement prevents proof-texting either image field.

proposed_units.title: Where Is Your King Now?
proposed_units.literary_form: ruin verdict and royal question-answer oracle
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Direct divine address to Israel moves from self-destruction/helper contrast to rhetorical questions about king and judges, then a first-person answer.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Ruin/helper line Hos.13.9; king/judges questions Hos.13.10; anger/wrath answer Hos.13.11.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.13.12 begins a stored-guilt and childbirth/death image sequence.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The question 'Where is your king now?' and reminder 'Give me a king and princes' receive the direct answer 'I have given ... and have taken', completing the royal oracle.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.13.9-13.11 preserves direct Israel address, help/save field, where-question, king/judges/princes terms, and give/take anger-wrath parallel; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The helper/save contrast introduces the king's inability to save, so Hos.13.9 is the rhetorical premise of the question-answer unit.

proposed_units.title: Stored Guilt at the Birth Opening, Death Addressed
proposed_units.literary_form: stored-guilt childbirth metaphor and death-Sheol question chain
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine/prophetic speech describes stored guilt, an unwise son at birth, and addresses Death and Sheol; the polarity and punctuation of Hos.13.14 are not decided.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Stored guilt Hos.13.12; labor/failed-birth metaphor Hos.13.13; ransom/redeem and Death/Sheol questions with compassion closure Hos.13.14.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.13.15 turns to east wind, dried spring, plunder, and Samaria's judgment.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: Stored-up guilt becomes labor pains and a son who fails to emerge; ransom/redeem clauses and direct addresses to Death/Sheol form the climax even though translation and punctuation affect its perceived direction.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.13.12-13.14 preserves stored/bound guilt, labor/son/womb field, ransom/redeem, Death/Sheol vocatives, and concealed-compassion close; marker evidence cannot select the punctuation or preferred reading.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: The Death/Sheol address is the climax of the childbirth-and-death movement, not a detachable promise or taunt; because its presentation remains translation-sensitive, retain the larger unit as a hold.

proposed_units.title: East Wind over the Spring and Samaria
proposed_units.literary_form: east-wind judgment and city lament
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Third-person judgment moves from Ephraim's fruitfulness to wind, drought, plunder, and Samaria's guilt and violent fall.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: East-wind drought/plunder Hos.13.15; Samaria guilt and war consequence Hos.13.16.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: WEB Hos.14.1 begins direct appeal, 'Israel, return to Yahweh your God'; in MT coordinates that appeal is Hos.14.2.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The east wind dries spring and fountain and plunders treasure; Samaria then bears guilt and falls by sword, completing the judgment before the imperative return summons.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.13.15-14.1 proves the WEB/MT chapter offset and preserves east-wind/dry/plunder plus Samaria-guilt/sword consequence; locators are evidence only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: In local WEB coordinates Hos.14.1 is already the imperative return summons, not the Samaria judgment found at MT Hos.14.1; using the chapter-shaped alternative would merge judgment with a genuine discourse reset.

proposed_units.title: Return with Words
proposed_units.literary_form: return appeal with supplied communal confession
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Prophetic imperative addresses Israel and instructs a communal speech to Yahweh concerning forgiveness, Assyria, horses, hand-made gods, and mercy.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Return-and-fall rationale Hos.14.1; take-words instruction and forgiveness petition Hos.14.2; renunciation and mercy confession Hos.14.3.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.14.4 changes from instructed human speech to a divine first-person healing response.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The repeated imperative 'return' and instruction 'Take words with you ... Tell him' require Hos.14.2-14.3 to stay with Hos.14.1; the supplied words end before 'I will heal'.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.14.2-14.4 preserves return imperatives, take/word/say instructions, first-person plural confession, and orphan-mercy closure; the crosswalk prevents a false seam after WEB Hos.14.1.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.14.1's return command is immediately elaborated by 'Take words ... and return'; separating it would atomize the summons from the prayer it supplies.

proposed_units.title: Healing, Dew, Roots, Shade, and Fruit
proposed_units.literary_form: divine healing response and flourishing image chain
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: Divine first-person response promises healing and freely given love, then describes Israel/Ephraim with dew, lily, Lebanon, olive, shade, grain, vine, wine, cypress, and fruit.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Healing/love Hos.14.4; dew-root-branch-fragrance growth Hos.14.5-14.6; shade/grain/vine renewal Hos.14.7; idol renunciation and cypress/fruit closure Hos.14.8.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Hos.14.9 leaves direct promise for a third-person wisdom colophon asking who is wise and prudent.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The divine 'I will heal ... I will love ... I will be like the dew' initiates one accumulating flourishing chain, and Hos.14.8's 'I answer ... take care ... from me your fruit' closes it.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.14.5-14.9 preserves first-person heal/love/anger turn, dew and plant vocabulary, Lebanon/fragrance repetitions, answer/watch, cypress, and fruit; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Hos.14.8 remains divine first-person speech and completes the idol-to-fruit answer, whereas Hos.14.9 alone has the wisdom question and righteous/rebellious contrast; the proposed alternative crosses the sharper form seam.

proposed_units.title: Who Is Wise to Understand the Ways?
proposed_units.literary_form: wisdom colophon
proposed_units.scene_speaker_addressee: A closing instructional voice addresses any wise/prudent hearer and generalizes the collection as right ways in which righteous and rebellious respond differently.
proposed_units.oracle_stanza_refrain: Two who-questions followed by a balanced ways/walk/stumble maxim.
proposed_units.discourse_reset: Final collection closure; no following Hosea discourse.
proposed_units.deciding_marker: The paired third-person questions 'Who is wise? Who is prudent?' and generalized maxim about the ways of Yahweh differ in voice and form from Hos.14.4-14.8's first-person healing promise.
proposed_units.local_marker_corroboration: OSHB/UXLC MT Hos.14.10 preserves the who-question pair, understand/know parallel, way plural, right/righteous, walk, rebel, and stumble balance; corroborative only.

rejected_exact_alternative.argument: Merging the colophon would erase the demonstrable shift from direct divine promise and first-person imagery to generalized wisdom address; this one-verse unit is form-driven, not fame-driven.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Superscription and Enacted Naming Cycle
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.literary_form: superscription plus three enacted signs and naming reversals
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Any child hit should offer the whole sign cycle, especially the Lo-Ammi-to-my-people reversal across the WEB chapter seam.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Marital Lawsuit and Restoration Diptych
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.literary_form: accusation-consequence movement answered by alluring-betrothal restoration
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Present judgment and restoration children with their diptych parent so neither half becomes the sole retrieval frame.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: The Go-Again Restoration Sign
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Keep command, enactment, direct address, and interpretation available as one parent even if later review adds children.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Land, Priest, People, and Leadership Lawsuit
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Hydrate local priest, cult, Judah-warning, and leadership accusations to the larger lawsuit so repeated knowledge/prostitution/stumbling language remains visible.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Alarm, Failed Return, Healing Hinge, and Political Indictment
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Mandatory for Hos.5.15-6.4 and Hos.6.11-7.2 hits; preserve the voice changes and the held cross-chapter hinge without flattening them.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Trumpets, Sowing and Reaping, Cult and Monarchy
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.literary_form: interlocking cult-monarchy accusation and consequence movements
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Keep sow/reap, harvest, vine, calf, king, exile, and prophet-hostility children inside the long judgment macro rather than retrieving metaphors alone.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Parental Recollection and Compassion
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.literary_form: care-refusal-consequence movement answered by compassion and return
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Mutually hydrate recollection/judgment and compassion/restoration so either child retains the deliberate turn at Hos.11.8.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Falsehood, Jacob, Merchant, and Prophet
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Preserve the Hos.11.12-12.1 accusation couplet and the later Jacob/prophet parallels under one parent; do not let chapter numbers route them independently.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Death, Kingship, Stored Guilt, and East-Wind Judgment
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Use the WEB/MT crosswalk. The strategy's Hos.13.1-14.1 parent is MT-shaped and equals WEB Hos.13.1-13.16; do not pull WEB Hos.14.1's return imperative into the judgment child.

macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.title: Return, Healing, Flourishing, and Wisdom Close
macro_parent_hydration_recommendations.hydration: Return summons, supplied confession, divine healing response, flourishing images, and wisdom colophon should remain mutually available while preserving the sharp Hos.14.8-14.9 form seam.

cross_chapter_seam_red_team.argument: Lo-Ammi's birth/name, direct reversal, gathered people, Jezreel reversal, and 'My people/My loved one' commands form one sign-reversal movement. The double 'Contend' at Hos.2.2 is the real lawsuit reset.

cross_chapter_seam_red_team.result: Three adjacent units: Hos.5.8-5.15, Hos.6.1-6.3, Hos.6.4-6.10.
cross_chapter_seam_red_team.argument: Divine withdrawal in Hos.5.15, communal first-person return speech in Hos.6.1-6.3, and divine double-vocative questions in Hos.6.4 are distinct voice/form moves; macro hydration preserves the call-response relationship.

The Judah harvest/restoration clause and 'When I would heal Israel' bridge the chapter. Hos.7.3's king/princes court scene is the clearer next reset. Exact punctuation/attachment remains a presentation hold.

cross_chapter_seam_red_team.result: Boundary after Hos.11.11; cross-chapter accusation Hos.11.12-12.1.
cross_chapter_seam_red_team.argument: The settling promise closes with 'says Yahweh'. Falsehood/deceit in Hos.11.12 continues as lies/desolation and Assyria/Egypt action in Hos.12.1 before the new controversy formula at Hos.12.2.

cross_chapter_seam_red_team.result: Hos.13.12-13.14 held; Hos.13.15-13.16 judgment; Hos.14.1-14.3 return summons.
cross_chapter_seam_red_team.argument: Childbirth/death language climaxes at Hos.13.14, east wind and Samaria finish judgment, and WEB Hos.14.1 begins the imperative appeal. The MT offset explains why strategy locators cross a chapter without authorizing a WEB chapter merge.
Hos.14.8 remains divine first-person answer/care/cypress/fruit speech; Hos.14.9 changes to paired third-person wisdom questions and a generalized ways maxim.

contested_presentation_questions.question: Should a presentation render Hos.6.11a as the prior indictment's close while still hydrating Hos.6.11b-7.2 as one restoration/healing hinge, or keep all three verses visibly together?
contested_presentation_questions.why_not_theology_or_identity: The question concerns punctuation, syntactic display, and retrieval hydration only.

contested_presentation_questions.question: Should Hos.9.7-9.8 be displayed as one or more voice-aligned lines inside the reckoning/watchman stanza while Hos.9.9 remains its Gibeah verdict?
contested_presentation_questions.why_not_theology_or_identity: No identity of the prophet/watchman is requested; only stanza and speaker-layout presentation is held.

contested_presentation_questions.question: How should punctuation and question/answer layout expose the relation among stored guilt, failed birth, ransom/redeem, Death/Sheol vocatives, and concealed compassion without splitting Hos.13.14 away?
